partes.p: (25 points) Suppose you observe a random variable $X \sim U[-\theta, \theta]$. You have only this one single observation.
Write down the likelihood function for $\lambda$ and a sample $X_{1}, \ldots, X_{n}$.

It can be shown that for $n$ i.i.d. draws $X_{1}, \ldots, X_{n}$ from an exponential distribution with failure rate $\lambda$, $Y_{n} := 2\lambda(X_{1} + X_{2} + \ldots + X_{n})$ follows a $\chi^{2}$ distribution with $2n$ degrees of freedom (this result is far from obvious and the math needed to derive this is beyond the scope of this class). In order to achieve a probability of a type-I error $\alpha = 0.1$, how do you choose the critical value on the sample mean in the test from part (d)? Do you reject the null hypothesis for the sample of size 8 given above?
